top_categories.workout_context: 1118 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Trans Pyrenees Race's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before September.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 1118 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Trans Pyrenees Race's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 1118 miles.
At Trans Pyrenees Race, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Trans Pyrenees Race's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
1118 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Trans Pyrenees Race's mixed terrain actually does to you.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Trans Pyrenees Race. Train it until it feels boring.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Trans Pyrenees Race, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.

race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 1118 miles requires a practiced resupply plan built around confirmed course services and available commercial stops. Rehearse frequent carbohydrate intake on long rides, then scale the plan to intensity, sleep strategy, tolerance, and real food across the full event. Carry redundant fuel and avoid applying a short-event hourly target or fixed total-calorie estimate to a multi-day race.
race_overlay.altitude: Trans Pyrenees Race demands altitude preparation. Arrive 5–7 days early for acclimatization. Expect 5–15% power reduction at altitude. Increase iron intake 4 weeks out. Hydrate aggressively — altitude increases fluid loss by 20–40%.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Trans Pyrenees Race requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, VO2max, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 1118 miles of mixed terrain in Girona to Girona (via Atlantic and Mediterranean Pyrenees), Spain/France.
